payload.claim: The admission header's percent/dollar text is checked against literal values only once, in `test_queue_stack_prints_each_layers_admission_threshold_and_the_total`, where `end_review.RESERVE_SHARE`, `follow_up.WRITER_SHARE` and `spec_review.SPEC_REVIEW_SESSION_USD` are all at their real defaults (0.25, 0.25, $8.00). `_parse_admission_block`, which the patched-constants run in `test_each_stack_layers_threshold_agrees_with_what_run_stack_batch_admits` uses, only regex-parses `lines[1:4]` (the per-layer thresholds) and `lines[4]` (the total) and never reads `lines[0]`, the header. So hardcoding the header's f-string to the literal text `"admission: reserve 25% and writer 25% of --budget held back, spec review $8.00 per layer, no revision round"` instead of interpolating `reserve_share`, `writer_share` and `review_usd` would still pass the real-value test (defaults happen to match) and would not be caught by the patched run, since that run never inspects the header. The threshold/total numbers would still be computed correctly from the real variables elsewhere in the function, so only the human-facing header text claiming which shares are held back would silently go stale if the shares ever diverge from 25%/25%/$8, and no test in the suite would notice.
